newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-DYNAMO MOSCOW RELISH TOP SPOT, SCENT DOUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DYNAMO MOSCOW RELISH TOP SPOT, SCENT DOUBLE.

text.p: It is early days yet but there is a scent of a footballing spring around Moscow's Dynamo stadium.

Russian soccer's most consistent under-achievers sit on top of the league for the first time in two years and captain and goalkeeper Andrei Smetanin, with five consecutive League and Cup clean sheets under his belt, has caught the whiff of success.

"If we play like we're playing now we can do the double," he told Reuters from the training ground on Monday after the club overtook Rotor Volgograd with a 1-0 home win at the weekend over 1996 runners-up Alania Vladikavkaz.
Funded by Stalin's secret police and personally overseen by the dictator's sinister henchman Lavrenti Beria, Dynamo dominated Soviet soccer before and after World War Two.

But though the generous Interior Ministry funding and 50,000-seat city centre ground remain, Dynamo last won the league in 1976 and a quarter-century has passed since Glasgow Rangers beat them 3-2 in the 1972 Cup Winners' Cup final.
Their only recent honour was the 1995 Russian Cup and a 6-1 first-round aggregate thrashing by Roma in this season's UEFA Cup summed up decades of disappointed international promise.

Smetanin attributed the current run of success, including a Cup semifinal berth against Zenit St Petersburg, to an influx of skilful youngsters and the weathered calm of trainer, Adamas Golodets, 63, who has been with the club for 30 years.
Belarussian international Andrei Ostrovsky has brought solidity to the defence while the midfield has benefited from the purchase of Vladimir Skokov from second division Taganrog.
The 23-year-old Sergei Grishin has also been on form, scoring on his international debut for Russia last month and making up for the loss of Dmitry Cheryshev to Sporting Gijon.
There is still a long way to go till the end of the season in November, however, and the players are being careful not to count their chickens.
Smetanin said the target was still the top three. Midfielder Andrei Kobelev, Saturday's goalscorer, would say only: "We could finish in a good position if we build on what we've done."

Dynamo fans remember the last time their team led the league, at about the same stage of the 1995 season after being runners-up to city rivals Spartak the previous year. That early promise was followed by an awful run and Dynamo finished fourth.

But with injury-hit champions Spartak in lacklustre form and pre-season second favourites Alania languishing in mid-table after 10 games, Dynamo fans are beginning to allow themselves hope that, at long last, this may be their year.
